events.summary: A calèche with four black horses overtakes the coach and collects Harker, whose luggage is transferred to it.
Dogs and wolves howl across the country as the calèche proceeds through the Pass, and the driver calms the horses.
A ring of wolves surrounds the calèche as the moon reveals them.
The driver drives the wolves back with a commanding gesture and climbs into the calèche.
A tall, old, clean-shaven man with a long white moustache, dressed entirely in black, who welcomes guests with courtly manners.
Count Dracula welcomes Harker into the castle and carries his luggage up to a prepared bedroom.
Harker finds the castle richly furnished yet strangely lacking mirrors and bells, and is left alone while the Count is absent.
Harker reads his notes on Carfax and the Count signs the papers for the Purfleet estate purchase.
The Count returns from his absence and talks with Harker through supper and into the dawn, then leaves at cockcrow.
The Count smashes the shaving glass by flinging it from the window onto the courtyard stones below.
Harker realises the castle is a prison and that he is a prisoner there.
Count Dracula talks at length with Harker about Transylvanian history and his family's warlike past.
Count Dracula has Harker write to Peter Hawkins and others, asking him to stay a month, and Harker reluctantly agrees.
Harker watches the Count climb out of his window and crawl down the castle wall.
Harker falls asleep on a couch in the old ladies' rooms, and what follows seems too real to be a dream.
Shows violent fury and superhuman strength, and claims Harker as his own, forbidding the women to touch him.
The Count seizes the fair woman by the neck and hurls her away, forbidding the women to touch Harker.
The women take the moving bag and vanish through the window in the moonlight, and Harker faints.
A terrible bag that the Count carries out of the castle at night, slung over his shoulder.
A distressed woman begs for her child at the castle gate, and the Count calls wolves into the courtyard.
Harker climbs along the castle wall to the Count's window and finds the room empty, then discovers the chapel vault.
The Count opens the great door to the wolves, but Harker begs him to shut it and wait for morning, and he does.
Harker finds the Count in his box gorged with blood and strikes at him with a shovel, but the Count's gaze stops him and the blow only cuts the forehead.
The Szgany and Slovaks arrive with carts, a door blows shut, and Harker is trapped again in the Count's room.
Renfield's birds have vanished and he has apparently eaten them, as the attendant reports.
A headland near Whitby, seen grey and misty from Mina's vantage, with sand-points stretching into the sea.
The coastguard reports a strange Russian ship drifting erratically as a storm approaches the coast.
The strange schooner drives into Whitby harbour with a dead man lashed to its wheel and runs aground on Tate Hill Pier.
The captain's log and bottled paper are read at the inquest, revealing a voyage of missing men and growing dread.
Mr. Swales is found dead on the seat in the churchyard, his neck broken and a look of horror on his face.
Mina finds Lucy missing from her bed, goes out in the night, and finds her asleep and half-clad on the East Cliff seat.
Mina wraps Lucy in a shawl and brings her home barefoot without being seen, and Lucy asks her to keep it secret.
Mr. Hawkins forwards news that Jonathan Harker has been ill, and Mina resolves to travel out to him.
Sister Agatha writes that Jonathan Harker has recovered enough to dictate a letter and will need weeks of rest.
Renfield escapes his room through the window and is pursued by Seward and the attendants.
Renfield is overpowered and restrained in a padded room.
Jonathan and Mina marry in Buda-Pesth, and Mina seals Jonathan's note-book in a wrapper as a pledge of trust.
Van Helsing visits Lucy with Seward, finds no functional cause, and asks to see her maid before deciding whether to return.
At sunset Renfield has a violent fit, falls calm, then releases his flies and says he is sick of them.
Seward urgently telegraphs Van Helsing to come at once after a terrible change in the patient.
Van Helsing notices a red mark on Lucy's throat beneath her black velvet band.
Seward and Van Helsing find Lucy near death and begin a second blood transfusion from Seward.
Van Helsing fixes a garlic wreath around Lucy's neck and forbids her to open the window or door.
Bersicker is found howling and tearing at his bars, with a tall stranger with red eyes nearby.
Writes a memorandum that she leaves to be seen, fearing she is dying of weakness.
Bersicker returns to the Zoo by himself and is locked back in his cage.
The maids are found drugged with laudanum, and Mina finds her mother's bottle emptied.
Mina, alone with her dead mother, hides a letter for Arthur in her breast, expecting to die that night.
Lies gravely weakened after a second attack, with two small mangled wounds at her throat.
Seward and Van Helsing break into the Westenra house and find Mrs. Westenra dead and Lucy near death.
Grief-stricken at Lucy's death; sobs uncontrollably.
Lucy speaks to Arthur in a hard, voluptuous voice and asks him to kiss her; Van Helsing physically stops him.
Lucy's breathing stops and she dies, with Van Helsing declaring it over.
Dead; her beauty has returned in death and her face looks alive, so that she seems a living woman rather than a corpse.
His father has recently died, and he is grieving both his father and Lucy.
Seward and Van Helsing view Lucy's body, which looks beautiful in death, and Van Helsing places wild garlic and a crucifix on her.
Mr. Marquand explains that Mrs. Westenra's will leaves the whole estate to Arthur, and he is pleased with the result.
Arthur kisses Lucy's dead hand and forehead, then says a farewell before the coffin is prepared.
In London, Harker recognises a tall dark stranger and is terrified; Mina takes him to rest in the Green Park.
After Lucy's burial, Arthur and Quincey leave for Ring while Van Helsing and Seward return to London.
Van Helsing reads Mina's typed record and is moved, thanking her warmly.
Mina is Jonathan's wife, who copied out his diary and gave Van Helsing the typed record, and who has been anxious about him.
Van Helsing reads the diaries with grave seriousness and is given the Count's history from Jonathan; in the paper he sees something that alarms him.
Van Helsing opens Lucy's leaden coffin and finds it empty.
Refuses to let Lucy's grave be mutilated and insists on protecting it, showing fierce grief and protectiveness toward her.
Van Helsing asks to cut off the head of Lucy's body, and Arthur bitterly refuses.
Appears as the dark-haired, blood-stained Un-Dead woman in grave clothes, her beauty turned to cruelty and wantonness.
Her eyes are unholy and full of hell-fire; she calls Arthur her husband and tries to draw him to her.
Uses wafers and consecrated bread to seal the tomb, and carries a long leather bag of tools into the churchyard.
The Westenra coffin is found empty, its lead lining cut open.
Accepts the task of driving the stake into Lucy's heart out of love, despite horror and despair.
Arthur drives the stake through Lucy's heart while the others pray.
Seward agrees to let Mina read his phonograph records and learn the full story of Lucy's death.
Mina listens to the phonograph cylinders and is overcome by the story of Lucy's death.
Harker traces the consignment of fifty cases of earth from Whitby to Carfax.
Arthur breaks down weeping on Mina's shoulder, and she comforts him like a mother with a child.
Mina tells Mr. Morris she will be his friend and kisses him; he calls her 'little girl' as Lucy once did.
Has been studying the diaries and letters and keeps a household in which Mina and Jonathan are staying.
Van Helsing learns the house Dracula bought lies next to Seward's, and says Mina should no longer take part in the danger.
Morris explains he shot at a bat that had settled on the window-sill.
Seward is called to Renfield, who is unusually eager to see him, and the group goes with him.
The party opens the chapel door and is struck by a foul stench of corruption and blood.
Rats swarm across the old house, and Lord Godalming calls in terriers to drive them away.
Mina takes a sleeping draught prepared by Dr. Seward and falls asleep.
A tea-room where Harker gets a cup of tea on his way back from the city.
Renfield is found lying face down on the floor, covered in blood, after a wild yell from his room.
Van Helsing trephines Renfield's skull to relieve the pressure, and Renfield briefly regains consciousness.
Renfield tells of a night when a presence at his window was let in after he gave it consent.
Renfield describes fighting the Count in his room and being flung down before the Count escapes under the door.
The group breaks into the Harkers' room and finds the Count feeding Mina from a wound in his breast, and he flees as a mist.
Renfield is found dead in his room, and Seward plans to certify it as misadventure.
Mina promises Van Helsing she will not die by her own hand while the Count lives.
The group enters Carfax and sanctifies the earth-filled chests by placing pieces of the Host inside them.
Lord Godalming and Quincey Morris go off to find a locksmith to break into the Piccadilly house, while the others wait in Green Park.
A locksmith opens the Piccadilly house door using a bunch of keys while Lord Godalming and Morris watch.
Godalming and Morris return and report that all twelve earth-boxes in the Carfax and Piccadilly lairs have been destroyed.
Van Helsing hypnotises Mina before dawn so she can speak freely.
As the room lightens, Van Helsing questions Mina in her trance.
Mina speaks in trance of a ship weighing anchor, then wakes and asks whether she spoke in her sleep.
Mina faints after Van Helsing tells her the Count can live for centuries and that she is mortal.
The group learns from the Doolittle's Wharf men that a tall pale man shipped a great box aboard the Czarina Catherine just before she sailed.
Van Helsing and Seward agree Mrs. Harker must be kept out of the group's council to protect against the Count's influence.
The group plans to leave for Varna by land on the 17th, arriving before the ship, and to carry Winchesters.
Mina makes Jonathan promise never to be told the group's plans against the Count, and he gives his word.
Is believed by the group to be travelling aboard the Czarina Catherine, sealed in a box.
Mrs. Harker asks the men to promise to kill her should she become too changed, and each man swears an oath.
The Czarina Catherine is reported entering Galatz at one o'clock.
The group arranges to take the early train to Galatz and to prepare letters, authority and consular help for the journey.
Mina tells the group she feels her soul freer since the Count's hold weakened, though she fears he may have used her knowledge.
Van Helsing proposes taking Mina overland toward the Count's castle while the men pursue by water.
Aboard the steam launch with Lord Godalming, pressing up the river in pursuit of the Count.
The launch continues up the river, with no sign yet of the boat carrying the box.
At the Borgo Pass Mina points out the road, having known it from Jonathan's diary, and they take the lonely by-road.
Mina sleeps through the day while Van Helsing drives, and they climb toward a castle on a high hill as sunset falls.
Van Helsing destroys the three Un-Dead women in their tombs at the chapel.
Van Helsing places the Wafer in Dracula's tomb, banishing him from it.
The gypsies flee after the Count's disappearance, leaving the group alone as the wolves withdraw.
Mr. Morris dies from his wound, after pointing to Mina's forehead and declaring the curse has passed away.
The group travels to Transylvania and revisits the old ground of their past terrors.

recaps.text: Harker travels by train from Munich through Vienna and Buda-Pesth, then east to Klausenburgh, noting the wild country and varied peoples. In Bistritz he is received at the Golden Krone and finds the Count's letter waiting, arranging his coach seat and carriage at the Borgo Pass. The landlord and his wife are frightened and evasive about the Count, and the old landlady pleads with Harker not to leave on the eve of St. George's Day. She presses a crucifix on him, which he wears despite his churchman's reservations.
recaps.title: CHAPTER I JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, an English solicitor's clerk, travels from Bistritz toward the Count's country, having been warned by the frightened Golden Krone landlady and given a crucifix. He rode the coach into the Borgo Pass, where passengers seemed to know a dark secret and offered him charms. A black calèche with a tall, bearded driver with red-glowing eyes collected him, and the night ride through wolf howls has begun, with the carriage turning off the main road toward an unknown destination.

Harker rides through green hills and mountains toward the Borgo Pass, admiring the scenery while his fellow passengers cross themselves at roadside shrines. At dusk the passengers grow excited and urge the driver on, then offer Harker charms and gifts as they enter the Pass. Harker rides through the night, and at midnight wolves and dogs howl; the driver calms the horses and turns down a narrow road to the right.
recaps.title: CHAPTER I JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: The driver's identity and reason for the journey remain unexplained.
recaps.title: CHAPTER I JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, an English solicitor's clerk, travelled from Bistritz into the Carpathians, warned by frightened locals and given a crucifix, and was collected by a strange driver for a night ride toward an unknown destination. He has now arrived at Castle Dracula, where the pale, aquiline Count Dracula welcomed him and left him alone while absent. Harker has supped, slept, and explored a library of English books, but he remains uneasy, notes the lack of servants and mirrors, and has found one door locked. The purpose of his visit, to explain a London estate purchase, is still unresolved.

The Count has left and Harker has explored the library, finding English books, magazines and reference works. A locked door opposite his room remains closed. Harker is still unsure of his situation and uneasy about his host.
recaps.title: CHAPTER II JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL—continued

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, an English solicitor's clerk, travelled from Bistritz into the Carpathians, warned by frightened locals and given a crucifix, and was collected for a night ride to Castle Dracula. There he met the pale, aquiline Count Dracula, who is keen to learn English and has bought the Carfax estate at Purfleet near London through Harker. The castle has no servants or mirrors and a locked door, and Harker has begun to suspect he is effectively alone with the Count. At the end of this passage Harker is uneasy, the Count's atlas marks Exeter and Whitby as well as London, and Harker is still trapped in the castle.

Jonathan Harker, an English solicitor's clerk, travelled into the Carpathians and was taken to Castle Dracula, where he met the pale Count Dracula, who has bought the Carfax estate at Purfleet near London through him. The castle has no servants or mirrors, and Harker has come to suspect he is alone with the Count. This morning the Count appeared behind him without a reflection, reacted with fury to Harker's cut and to the crucifix, and smashed the shaving glass. Harker found every door locked and now knows he is a prisoner, with the Count's atlas marking Exeter and Whitby as well as London.

Harker breakfasts alone, as the Count is nowhere to be found and has not been seen eating or drinking. Exploring, he finds a southern view over a precipice and forests, but every door is locked and bolted. He concludes the castle is a prison and he is a prisoner.
recaps.title: CHAPTER II JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL—continued

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, an English solicitor's clerk, travelled to Transylvania and was taken to Castle Dracula, where the pale Count Dracula has bought the Carfax estate at Purfleet near London through him. Harker found every door locked and realised he is a prisoner, with no servants and an unseen Count who casts no reflection and once reacted violently to the crucifix. He has decided to conceal his fears and watch closely. The Count has now pressed him to write letters extending his stay by a month, and Harker has complied, while the Count's motives remain unknown.

That night the Count talks proudly of the Szekely people and the Dracula family's battles against the Magyars, Turks and others, speaking as if he had been present at them. Next day the Count questions Harker on English legal practice, agencies, and consigning goods to ports such as Exeter-area and northern towns, showing wide knowledge.
recaps.title: CHAPTER III JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL—continued

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, an English solicitor's clerk, is held prisoner at Castle Dracula in Transylvania by Count Dracula, who bought property near London through him and has no reflection. The Count has forced Harker to write letters extending his stay and makes him suspicious and afraid. Harker has seen the Count climb down the castle wall like a lizard and has found the main door locked with its key missing, probably in the Count's room. Harker has now slept in the old ladies' rooms, and his sense of reality is shaken by what he experienced there.

Jonathan Harker, an English solicitor's clerk, is a prisoner at Castle Dracula in Transylvania, held by Count Dracula, who bought English property through him and casts no reflection. Harker has been forced to write letters extending his stay and has seen the Count climb the castle wall; the main door is locked and its key missing. The Count talks proudly of Szekely and Dracula family battles and questions Harker on English legal and trade practice. Harker has slept in the old ladies' rooms, where three women nearly kissed him until the Count violently drove them off, promising Harker to them later, and they fled with a moving bag. Harker has fainted, shaken and unsure of what is real, and the Count's intentions toward him remain unresolved.

In the moonlit old room, three women approach Harker, whisper, and lean in to kiss his throat with sharp teeth. Harker lies in an agony of desire and fear. The Count bursts in with furious rage, grabs the fair woman, and drives all of them back, declaring Harker belongs to him. The Count promises they may kiss Harker later, then orders them away because he must wake Harker for work.
recaps.title: CHAPTER III JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL—continued

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker is a prisoner at Castle Dracula, held by Count Dracula, who has bought English property through him. The Count forced Harker to write letters extending his stay, took his papers and suit, and has been seen wearing those clothes. Harker has been menaced by three women and has seen the Count leave with the bag. A Szgany band camps in the courtyard and a Slovak wagon delivered heavy boxes. A distressed woman begs at the gate for her child, and the Count has summoned wolves. Harker remains locked in his room, unable to escape or send word home.

Jonathan Harker is a prisoner at Castle Dracula, held by Count Dracula, who has bought English property through him. The Count forged Harker's letters, took his papers and clothes, and has been seen wearing them. Three women have menaced Harker, a Szgany band and Slovak wagon are at the castle, and the Count commands wolves. Harker has found the Count's room and the chapel vault where the Count lies in an earth-filled box. The front door is bolted again, and Harker is heading back down to the chapel, still seeking the key.
Harker wakes at dawn, finds the front door bolted again, and climbs back to the Count's room, planning to find the key. He descends again toward the chapel, knowing where the monster lies.
recaps.title: CHAPTER IV JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL—continued

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker is a prisoner at Castle Dracula, where Count Dracula forged his letters, took his papers and clothes, and plans to move to England. The Count's coffin-like boxes of earth are being shipped out by Szgany and Slovak carters. Harker has seen the Count gorged with blood in his box and wounded him with a shovel, but was stopped by his gaze. Now he is trapped again in the Count's room after the carts depart, alone with the three women, and resolves to climb down the castle wall to escape.

Harker raises the lid of the great box and finds the Count gorged with fresh blood, looking younger, with no sign of the key. Overcome with horror, he strikes at the Count with a shovel, but the Count's eyes stop him and only a gash is made. Hearing the Szgany and Slovaks approach with song and wheels, Harker runs back to the Count's room intending to escape. He hears the great door unlocked and many feet tramp inside, then a gust of wind slams the stair door and traps him. Harker writes as the boxes are nailed shut and the carts leave, leaving him alone with the three women. He resolves to climb the castle wall, taking gold, and escape home, though he is despairing. He hears the carts go and resolves to scale the wall, taking gold, writing a farewell to Mina before the attempt.
recaps.title: CHAPTER IV JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL—continued

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker is a prisoner at Castle Dracula, where Count Dracula forged his letters, took his papers, and is shipping earth-filled boxes to England. Harker wounded the Count with a shovel, was trapped in the castle, and resolved to climb down the wall and escape. In Whitby, Mina waits anxiously for word from Jonathan, whose last letter seemed strange, while Lucy's sleepwalking worries her family. Dr. Seward studies his patient Renfield, whose appetite for devouring living things he finds alarming. Mina has heard nothing from Jonathan since his brief letter, and Arthur's visit has been postponed.

Dr. Seward records Renfield's escalating collecting of flies, spiders, sparrows, and his request for a cat, and concludes he is a life-devouring maniac. Mina's journal reports a curt letter from Jonathan sent from Castle Dracula, which she finds unlike him, and Lucy's sleepwalking has been prompting Mina to lock the door at night. Mina notes Mr. Holmwood's visit has been delayed, and Lucy seems to be watching her in her sleep, searching for the room key.
recaps.title: CHAPTER VI MINA MURRAY’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker is a prisoner at Castle Dracula, where Count Dracula forged his letters, took his papers, and is shipping earth-filled boxes to England. Harker wounded the Count and resolved to escape by climbing down the castle wall. In Whitby, Mina waits anxiously for word from Jonathan, whose last letter seemed strange, while Lucy's sleepwalking worries her family. Dr. Seward studies his patient Renfield, whose appetite for devouring living things alarms him. At the end of this passage, Mina still has no news of Jonathan, Mr. Swales has spoken of his approaching death, and a strange Russian ship is battling a coming storm off Whitby.

Mina writes in her journal of a grey, stormy day at Whitby, with fishing boats hurrying home and no news of Jonathan. Old Mr. Swales sits with Mina and speaks gently of death, saying he is ready to die and that death may be near. The coastguard joins her and points out a strange Russian ship that cannot decide whether to run north or put into harbour. The coastguard expects to learn more of the ship by the next day.
recaps.title: CHAPTER VI MINA MURRAY’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker is a prisoner at Castle Dracula, where Count Dracula forged his letters, took his papers, and is shipping earth-filled boxes to England; Harker wounded the Count and resolved to escape down the castle wall. In Whitby, Mina waits anxiously for word from Jonathan, whose last letter seemed strange, while Lucy's sleepwalking worries her family. Dr. Seward studies his patient Renfield, whose appetite for devouring living things alarms him. Mr. Swales has spoken of his approaching death, and a strange Russian schooner has now been wrecked in Whitby harbour during a sudden storm, its dead steersman lashed to the wheel and a large dog escaped onto the cliff.

A sudden storm breaks over Whitby after a calm, sultry evening, with huge waves and sea-fog sweeping the harbour piers. The searchlight on East Cliff guides boats to safety and picks out a schooner with all sails set, driving toward the reef.
recaps.title: CHAPTER VII CUTTING FROM “THE DAILYGRAPH,” 8 AUGUST

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker is a prisoner at Castle Dracula, where Count Dracula forged his letters, took his papers, and is shipping earth-filled boxes to England; Harker wounded the Count and resolved to escape down the castle wall. In Whitby, Mina waits anxiously for word from Jonathan, whose last letter seemed strange, while Lucy's sleepwalking worries her. Dr. Seward studies his patient Renfield, whose appetite for devouring living things alarms him. A strange Russian schooner was wrecked in Whitby harbour during a storm, its dead steersman lashed to the wheel and a large dog escaped onto the cliff. After the sea-captain's funeral, Mr. Swales is found dead on the bench, and Lucy and Mina plan a long walk to tire Lucy out; Jonathan's whereabouts remain unknown.

On the morning after the storm, Lucy and Mina go down to the harbour, where huge waves force their way through the narrow mouth. Mina worries about Jonathan's whereabouts and fears for his safety. At the funeral of the dead sea-captain, boats follow the coffin from Tate Hill Pier to the churchyard, and the women watch from their usual seat. Lucy is restless and uneasy. Mr. Swales is found dead on the seat that morning, with an expression of fear. A dog that refuses to come to its master is kicked and placed on a tombstone, where it cowers, and Lucy is deeply distressed. Mina decides to tire Lucy with a long walk to Robin Hood's Bay and back, hoping to stop her sleepwalking.
recaps.title: CHAPTER VII CUTTING FROM “THE DAILYGRAPH,” 8 AUGUST

recaps.text: In the night Mina finds Lucy gone from her bed and searches the town, eventually finding her asleep on the churchyard seat at the East Cliff. Something dark seemed to bend over Lucy there before Mina reached her; Mina covers her, wakes her, and leads her home unseen. Lucy seems healthier the next day, though Mina accidentally pricks her throat with a safety-pin; Lucy begs Mina to tell no one, and Mina agrees. On the following nights Mina locks the door and keeps the key on her wrist, and Lucy is restless but sleeps on, while a bat flits over the harbour.
recaps.title: CHAPTER VIII MINA MURRAY’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker is a prisoner at Castle Dracula, where Count Dracula forged his letters and is shipping earth-filled boxes to England; Harker wounded the Count and planned an escape. In Whitby, Mina waits for word from Jonathan while Lucy sleepwalks, and Lucy's mother is secretly dying of a weak heart. A wrecked Russian schooner and the death of Mr. Swales have unsettled the town. Lucy's throat wounds will not heal and she grows weaker, while Mina learns that Jonathan has been ill in Buda-Pesth and is preparing to travel out to him.

On the East Cliff, Lucy remarks on red eyes at sunset, and Mina sees Lucy asleep at her window with something bird-like beside her. Mrs. Westenra confides to Mina that her heart is failing and she may die within months; Lucy's engagement to Arthur is announced happily. Lucy seems better, but Mina finds her weaker and fainting at the window, and the throat wounds remain open and white-edged. Billington & Son's letters arrange delivery of fifty boxes to Carfax, and Carter, Paterson confirm delivery and return change. Jonathan's news finally arrives through Sister Agatha, who reports his illness; Mina prepares to leave to nurse him.
recaps.title: CHAPTER VIII MINA MURRAY’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker is a prisoner at Castle Dracula, where Count Dracula forged his letters and ships earth-filled boxes to England; Harker wounded the Count and planned escape. In Whitby, Mina waits for word from Jonathan while Lucy sleepwalks and grows weaker, and Lucy's mother is secretly dying. Mina has learned that Jonathan is ill in Buda-Pesth and is preparing to go nurse him. Renfield, a patient of Dr. Seward who keeps living creatures, has escaped to the chapel grounds of Carfax, where he served a Master; he is now restrained and raving that the Master is coming.

Jonathan Harker escaped Castle Dracula and is ill in Buda-Pesth, where Mina prepares to nurse him. Lucy Westenra is weakened by a mysterious illness, and her mother is dying. Dr. Seward's patient Renfield, who keeps living creatures, has had violent fits at noon and sunset and is now restrained and raving about a Master. Seward has telegraphed Van Helsing to come at once after a sudden terrible decline in his patient on 6 September.

Seward records that his patient had a violent outburst at noon, then grew melancholy and quiet. Later the patient seemed happy, catching flies and asking for more sugar, which Seward granted. At midnight another fit at sunset left the patient calm again, and he released his flies and rejected his fly-keeping. Seward wonders whether the sun affects this man at certain times, and telegraphs Van Helsing, reporting improvement and then a sudden terrible decline on 6 September.
recaps.title: CHAPTER IX

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker escaped Castle Dracula and is ill in Buda-Pesth, where Mina nurses him. Lucy Westenra is weakened by a mysterious illness and her mother is anxious for her. Dr. Seward's patient Renfield has had violent fits and raves about a Master. On 7 September Van Helsing arrives and Lucy receives a blood transfusion from Arthur, who is sent home to rest. A red mark on Lucy's throat has been noticed but not yet explained.

On 7 September Van Helsing arrives and advises Seward to keep the truth from Arthur, while urging careful records of all observations. Arthur arrives unexpectedly, eager to help, and Van Helsing asks him to donate blood, which is done after Lucy is given a narcotic.
recaps.title: CHAPTER X

recaps.text: Seward sits up with Lucy, who sleeps deeply and says she fears sleep, and he promises to wake her if bad dreams come. On 10 September Seward finds Lucy deathly pale and unconscious; Van Helsing revives her with a second transfusion from Seward and gives morphia. Lucy wakes weaker but chatty, and Seward signals her silence when her mother praises him.
recaps.title: CHAPTER X

recaps.text: On 11 September the narrator visits Hillingham and finds Lucy improved. Van Helsing presents a parcel of garlic flowers as medicine, which Lucy mocks as common garlic. Van Helsing reacts sternly, then gently, and hangs garlic about Lucy's room and neck, warning her not to open the windows or door. He is confident of her safety, and the narrator feels uneasy.
recaps.title: CHAPTER X

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker escaped Castle Dracula and is recovering in Buda-Pesth under Mina's care. Lucy Westenra has been weakened by a mysterious illness that has left a mark on her throat, and Van Helsing, with Seward and Arthur, has given her blood transfusions and used garlic as protection. Her mother removed the garlic flowers, which Van Helsing found alarming. Lucy has since recovered and Van Helsing has gone to Amsterdam. Separately, the wolf Bersicker has escaped from the Zoölogical Gardens after a strange man stirred the animals, and the keeper has been interviewed about it.

Seward visits Hillingham with Van Helsing, who finds Lucy's mother has removed the garlic flowers from Lucy's room, causing him to despair. Van Helsing insists Seward operate, performs another blood transfusion, and arranges for Lucy to be watched over. Lucy writes of four days of peace, with the frightening noises gone and garlic brought from Haarlem each day; Van Helsing leaves for Amsterdam. A Pall Mall Gazette reporter interviews the Zoölogical Gardens keeper Thomas Bilder about the escaped wolf Bersicker, who was disturbed by a stranger the day before.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XI

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker escaped Castle Dracula and is recovering in Buda-Pesth under Mina's care. Lucy Westenra was weakened by a mysterious illness, treated with blood transfusions and garlic, and has since recovered before Van Helsing left for Amsterdam. The wolf Bersicker escaped the Zoo and has returned on his own, cut and bloodied, and is locked back up. Seward was cut by a violent patient and is exhausted. Van Helsing urged Seward to watch Lucy closely; a wolf broke into Lucy's room, and her mother died of fright while Lucy fell into a spell.

Thomas Bilder tells the reporter that the escaped wolf Bersicker was likely hiding and suggests a stray child might be lost to it. Bersicker comes back alone, bloodied and cut from broken glass, and Bilder locks him up and feeds him. Seward is attacked by a patient who cuts his wrist and licks up the blood, repeating that blood is life; Seward is weakened and exhausted. Van Helsing telegraphs urging Seward to watch Lucy closely; Seward sets out for London with the phonograph cylinder.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XI

recaps.text: Mina wakes in her room to a tolling bell, howling dogs and a nightingale, and finds the maids fled with fright after seeing her mother's body. She sends the maids to the dining-room for wine and goes looking for them when they do not return. She finds all four maids drugged on the floor, the sherry laced with laudanum and her mother's medicine bottle empty. Alone with the body and hearing a wolf outside, she writes a farewell to Arthur and hides it in her breast.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XI

recaps.text: Seward arrives at Hillingham early and finds the house locked and silent, so he and Van Helsing break in through a kitchen window. They find four drugged maids and Mrs. Westenra dead, with Lucy alive but barely breathing with fresh marks on her throat. Using brandy, heat and a bath, they revive Lucy, and Quincey Morris arrives with a telegram from Arthur and offers his blood for another transfusion. Lucy slowly recovers and sinks into morphia-induced sleep, while Van Helsing reads a private paper that fell from her breast and keeps its contents from Seward. Seward arranges the death certificate listing heart disease, avoiding an inquest, and goes to the undertaker while Quincey waits to speak with him.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XII DR. SEWARD’S DIARY

recaps.text: Quincey Morris asks Seward to be told what is wrong with Lucy and says he has given his blood, guessing Arthur was the first donor. Lucy wakes, weeps for her mother, and tears up Van Helsing's paper in her sleep before he takes the pieces. On the nineteenth Lucy grows weaker; Arthur arrives by evening and rallies her briefly, and Seward despairs that she may not survive the next day. Hennessey reports that Renfield attacked a carrier's man at the empty house next door and was overpowered and restrained.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XII DR. SEWARD’S DIARY

recaps.text: Harker is recovering in Buda-Pesth, and Mina is anxious about him and about Lucy. Lucy, weakened by a mysterious illness, has been treated with blood transfusions, garlic, and watchful care under Seward and Van Helsing. Renfield was overpowered after attacking a carrier. Lucy has now died at dawn after a frightening change, with Van Helsing warning that the death is only the beginning.

Seward relieves Van Helsing at Lucy's bedside, while Arthur sleeps and Seward watches the garlic-hung room and a bat outside. Lucy alternately sleeps in a stertorous state, pushing away the garlic, and wakes, clutching it to her. At dawn Van Helsing finds the throat wounds have disappeared, and he judges that Lucy is dying. Arthur is woken; Lucy briefly wakes, then in a changed voice asks him to kiss her, and Van Helsing violently stops him.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XII DR. SEWARD’S DIARY

recaps.text: Harker is recovering in Buda-Pesth and Mina is anxious for him and for Lucy. Lucy, weakened by a mysterious illness, was treated with transfusions and garlic under Seward and Van Helsing, and has died at dawn after a frightening change; Van Helsing warns her death is only the beginning. Her funeral is set for the next day, and Van Helsing has gathered her papers and proposed a secret operation on her body, which he has now dropped. Arthur has inherited the estate and is grieving his father and Lucy. The doctors now wait, with Van Helsing keeping secrets and Arthur in grief, and the situation unresolved.

The funeral is arranged for the next day so Lucy and her mother can be buried together, and Seward handles the formalities with the undertaker's staff. Van Helsing searches Lucy's papers and finds letters, memoranda and a new diary, but says nothing of them yet. Seward writes to Mrs. Westenra's solicitor, and the two men view Lucy's beautiful corpse, where Van Helsing places garlic and a crucifix. Van Helsing asks Seward for post-mortem knives, intending to behead Lucy and remove her heart, and insists on secrecy and trust; Seward promises to help. The next morning Van Helsing reveals the crucifix was stolen and recovered, and the knives will not be needed. Mr. Marquand explains the will leaves everything to Arthur, and Arthur, grieving his father and Lucy, breaks down in Seward's arms.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XIII DR. SEWARD’S DIARY—continued.

recaps.text: Harker recovers in Buda-Pesth while Mina worries for him. Lucy, weakened by a mysterious illness, was treated with transfusions and garlic and has died, after which Van Helsing warned her death is only the beginning. Lucy and her mother are buried, and Arthur inherits the estate and grieves. Van Helsing keeps Lucy's papers and his own counsel. In London Jonathan believes he saw the Count, and Mina plans to learn the truth of his journey.

Arthur, grieving, looks at Lucy's dead face and says goodbye, then the undertaker's men prepare the coffin. At dinner Van Helsing offers to trust Arthur further, asking to keep Lucy's papers, which Arthur allows. Walking in London, Jonathan sees a tall dark man with pointed teeth staring at a girl, and believes he is the Count. After resting in the park, Jonathan forgets the episode, while Mina resolves to read his journal. A telegram from Van Helsing reports that Mrs. Westenra died five days earlier and Lucy the day before, and both have been buried. Mina grieves for them and for Arthur.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XIII DR. SEWARD’S DIARY—continued.

recaps.text: Harker recovered in Buda-Pesth while Mina worried for him. Lucy, weakened by a mysterious illness, was treated with transfusions and garlic and died, and Van Helsing warned her death is only the beginning. Lucy and her mother are buried, and Arthur inherits the Westenra estate and grieves. Van Helsing keeps Lucy's papers and his own counsel. Arthur and Quincey have gone to Ring, while Van Helsing and Seward are back in London, Van Helsing planning to return and stay with Seward. Hampstead children are being lured away by a 'bloofer lady' and found wounded in the throat.

Jonathan recovered in Buda-Pesth after a terrible ordeal involving the Count, and Mina has been worried about him while he works away. Lucy has died, and Van Helsing, who treated her, has come to Exeter to examine Lucy's sleepwalking and the cliff incident with Mina. Mina has given him her typed record and he is grateful. Van Helsing still keeps Lucy's papers and his own counsel, and the wider danger connected to the Count remains unresolved.

Van Helsing arrives and Mina recognises his noble bearing. He explains that Lucy's diary mentions Mina saving her during sleepwalking on the cliff. Mina first teases him by offering the shorthand diary, then gives him her typed copy. While Mina goes to order lunch, Van Helsing reads the record and returns excited, thanking her and offering future help. Mina demurs that he does not know her well.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XIV MINA HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Jonathan recovered from brain fever in Buda-Pesth after his ordeal with the Count and is now back home with Mina in Exeter. Lucy has died, and Van Helsing, who treated her, has taken up the investigation. Mina gave Van Helsing her typed copy of Jonathan's journal, which convinced him that the account is true. Jonathan and Mina have now met Van Helsing, who asked Jonathan for more of his history. Van Helsing has left for London after reading alarming news in the Westminster Gazette, and the danger connected to the Count remains unresolved.
Van Helsing stays overnight in Exeter, then lunches with Mina and speaks warmly of her character. Mina sends word for breakfast the next morning, as Jonathan is returning home.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XIV MINA HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Jonathan recovered from brain fever in Buda-Pesth after his ordeal with the Count and is now back at home with Mina in Exeter. Lucy has died, and Van Helsing, who treated her, has taken up the investigation. Mina gave Van Helsing her typed copy of Jonathan's journal, which convinced him of its truth. Van Helsing has returned from Exeter with a newspaper report of children found with punctured throats at Hampstead. He has told Harker that Lucy herself made the wounds, and the nature of the danger, and what must be done, remains unresolved.

Van Helsing returns from Exeter in high spirits of purpose and shows Harker a newspaper report about children found with punctured throats at Hampstead. Harker sees the likeness to Lucy's wounds, but Van Helsing says the cause is not the same directly and presses him to accept mysteries beyond science. Van Helsing reveals that Lucy herself made the wounds on the children, a worse truth than Harker expected, leaving him stunned.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XIV MINA HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, recovered from brain fever and now at home with Mina in Exeter, has joined Van Helsing and Dr. Seward in a hunt against the Un-Dead. Lucy died and was buried, and Van Helsing, believing she is Un-Dead, has opened her tomb to find her body unchanged. Van Helsing has watched the churchyard alone and asked Arthur and Quincey for a promise before he acts. Harker and Seward have doubts, and the plan to destroy Lucy and find the Count is unresolved.

Harker and Van Helsing open Lucy's tomb in daylight and find her body unchanged and beautiful, with sharper teeth and red lips. Van Helsing decides not to act yet, judging that Arthur must be told first, and says Harker must return to the asylum.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XV DR. SEWARD’S DIARY—continued.

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, recovered and home with Mina in Exeter, has joined Van Helsing and Dr. Seward against the Un-Dead. Lucy died and was buried, and Van Helsing believes she has become Un-Dead. Van Helsing opened her tomb in daylight and found her body unchanged, with sharper teeth and red lips. Van Helsing now asks Arthur and Quincey to join a secret night visit to the churchyard and to the tomb. Arthur reluctantly agrees to go and wait, though he is still horrified by the plan to open the coffin and mutilate Lucy's body. The plan to destroy Lucy and to find the Count remains unresolved.
Arthur agrees to the terms but then angrily objects to Van Helsing's plan to open Lucy's coffin. Van Helsing says Lucy may be Un-Dead and asks to cut off her head, which Arthur furiously refuses.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XV DR. SEWARD’S DIARY—continued.

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, recovered and home with Mina in Exeter, has joined Van Helsing and Dr. Seward against the Un-Dead. Lucy died and was buried, and Van Helsing believes she has become Un-Dead. Van Helsing opened the tomb by day and found her body unchanged, with sharper teeth and red lips. The group, with Arthur and Quincey, watched the tomb at night and saw Lucy, the Un-Dead woman, feeding on a child and fleeing from Van Helsing's crucifix and consecrated wafers. Van Helsing and the others have resealed the tomb and plan a return the following night, with the Count still unfound and the work of destroying Lucy unfinished.

Van Helsing leads the group into the Westenra tomb, where Lucy's coffin is found empty, shocking Arthur and the others. Van Helsing explains that he removed his protective garlic and sealed the tomb each time with consecrated wafers, and that he saw nothing the night before. The group waits in hiding, then sees a dark-haired woman in grave clothes carrying a child, revealed as Lucy with blood on her lips. Lucy hurls the child down, calls to Arthur to come to her, and is held back by Van Helsing's crucifix before she slips into the tomb. Van Helsing asks Arthur for leave to continue, and Arthur consents in despair; Van Helsing reseals the tomb and takes the child to be found by the police.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XVI DR. SEWARD’S DIARY—continued

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, home with Mina in Exeter, has joined Van Helsing and Dr. Seward against the Un-Dead. Lucy died, was buried, and became Un-Dead, feeding on children and fleeing Van Helsing's protections. The group watched the tomb and saw her return with blood on her lips. In this passage Arthur staked Lucy in the tomb, and her body was laid to rest with garlic in its mouth and the coffin sealed. Van Helsing has called the group to meet in two nights and plans his next moves, while the Count remains unfound and the greater quest ahead is unresolved.

Van Helsing opens Lucy's coffin in the tomb and lays out his tools: a soldering iron, a lamp, knives, a charred wooden stake and a hammer. Van Helsing explains the curse of the Un-Dead and asks who will drive the stake, and Arthur volunteers despite his terror. Arthur drives the stake into Lucy's heart while the others read prayers; her body writhes and then falls still. Van Helsing asks his companions to join the search for the author of their sorrow, and they promise to continue to the end.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XVI DR. SEWARD’S DIARY—continued

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, home with Mina in Exeter, has joined Van Helsing and Dr. Seward against the Un-Dead, and Lucy has died, been buried and become Un-Dead before being staked in her tomb. Van Helsing has called the group to meet again and plans his next moves while the Count remains unfound. Mina has arrived in London and Seward has allowed her to listen to his phonograph diary and type its contents. Van Helsing is at Whitby seeking more information and is expected to return the following day to join them.

Van Helsing has called the group together and is expected back from Whitby, while the Count remains at large. Lucy has died and been staked in her tomb, and Van Helsing directs the search for the Count. Harker and Mina have typed and ordered all the diaries and documents into a single chronological record. Harker has confirmed that fifty boxes of earth from the Count's ship were delivered to Carfax. Lord Godalming and Mr. Morris have now read the compiled papers, and the group awaits Van Helsing's return to plan their next move.

Mina types Seward's phonograph cylinders into three copies and borrows old evening newspapers to look for clues. Seward keeps watch over Renfield, whose calm mood he finds suspicious. In London, Harker traces the boxes from King's Cross to Carfax, where a carter describes the dusty, frightening house. Harker concludes all the boxes are now at Carfax. Mina reports that she and Harker have finished putting the papers in order. Lord Godalming and Mr. Morris arrive early, and Mina gives each of them a copy to read.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XVII DR. SEWARD’S DIARY—continued

recaps.text: Lord Godalming, grieving over Lucy, breaks down in front of Mina, who sits with him and comforts him like a sister. He weeps on her shoulder, and she strokes his hair; he thanks her and asks to be her brother, and she promises to let him know if she ever needs help. Mina tells Morris she will be his friend and will know later why she speaks; he kisses her hand, she kisses him, and he calls her 'little girl' before going to Arthur in the study.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XVII DR. SEWARD’S DIARY—continued

recaps.text: Van Helsing has gathered Harker, Mina, Lord Godalming, Dr. Seward and Morris to plan the campaign against Count Dracula, whose nature and limits he has set out. The group joined hands in a solemn compact and is now deciding how to trace the earth-filled boxes, fifty of which were delivered to Carfax. A pistol shot broke the window; Morris explained he fired at a bat, and the group's search for the boxes remains unresolved.

Van Helsing describes the vampire's nature, strengths and limits, drawing on tradition and what the group has seen. He explains his belief that the Count may be the historical Dracula and outlines ways to destroy him. He notes the nosferatu's power to grow stronger and reach beyond death. The group pledges itself to the struggle, joining hands around the golden crucifix. Van Helsing proposes next to establish whether all fifty boxes of earth remain at Carfax. Before he can finish, a pistol shot shatters the window. Morris returns and explains he had shot at a bat on the sill, which he has been doing lately whenever he sees one. Van Helsing asks whether he hit it, and the question is left as the passage ends.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XVIII DR. SEWARD’S DIARY

recaps.text: Van Helsing has gathered Harker, Mina, Lord Godalming, Dr. Seward and Morris to plan the campaign against Count Dracula, whose nature and limits he has set out. The group has armed itself and entered the Count's old house at Carfax to search for the earth-filled boxes. They have found twenty-nine of fifty boxes left, and the rats have been driven off by the dogs. The party has searched the house and found no trace of the Count, and the question of the missing boxes is unresolved.

The party enters the old house and counts the earth chests, finding only twenty-nine of the fifty left. Harker briefly imagines the Count's face in the passage, but finds no one there and says nothing. The chamber fills with rats, and Lord Godalming opens the iron-bound door and whistles up three terriers. The dogs drive the rats away, and the party searches the house, finding only dust and Harker's own earlier footprints. At dawn Van Helsing locks the hall-door and pockets the key as they leave.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XIX JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: The group has entered the Count's old house at Carfax, counted the earth-boxes and driven off the rats, but the Count himself is not found and some boxes are missing. Van Helsing has decided Mina must be kept out of the dangerous work, and Harker has resolved to hide the night's events from her. Renfield, the disturbed asylum patient, has refused to talk to Van Helsing. The men are now tracing the missing boxes, and the Count remains at large with the search unresolved.

The group entered the old house at Carfax, counted the earth-boxes and drove off the rats, but the Count is still at large and some boxes are missing. Van Helsing has kept Mina out of the dangerous work, and Harker has hidden the night's events from her. Harker has gone to the Purfleet agents to learn about the property, and Lord Godalming awaits their reply. Renfield continues to show unsettling, half-rational talk about life and souls, which Seward finds suspicious.

Harker returns to Purfleet, finds the others at home, and reads them his diary of the day's discovery. Van Helsing says the house may hold the missing boxes, and Morris asks how they will get inside; Godalming plans to wait for Mitchell's reply.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XX JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: The group entered the old house at Carfax, counted the earth-boxes and drove off the rats, but the Count is still at large and some boxes are missing. Van Helsing has kept Mina out of the dangerous work, and Harker has hidden the night's events from her. Harker has been following a clue about the property and reported back. Mitchell, Sons & Candy have confirmed the Piccadilly house was bought by a foreign count paying in cash. Renfield, whose moods seem tied to the Count, has been found bloodied on his floor after a yell, and Seward has rushed to him; his condition and cause remain unresolved.

Seward finds Renfield on the floor in a pool of blood with severe facial wounds and apparent spinal and paralysis injuries, and the attendant Simmons is bewildered by the injuries. Renfield says Mrs. Harker seemed changed when she visited him that afternoon, and the listeners react with grim unease.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XXI DR. SEWARD’S DIARY

recaps.text: The group has been hunting the Count, who has taken Mina's blood and has been seen in the Harkers' room. Van Helsing and the others broke in and drove him off, though he escaped as mist. Harker and Mina are shaken; Mina is wounded and ashamed. The burned papers and cylinders are a loss, though a second copy of the records survives in Seward's safe. Renfield is found dead, and Morris saw a bat fly west toward the dawn, leaving the Count's whereabouts unknown.
Mina's shame about her blood is answered by Harker's refusal to let her be cast off. Godalming holds back something but is not pressed.

Renfield is dead, the Carfax earth-chests have been sanctified, and the Piccadilly house was searched. The Count is believed to have fled London by sea aboard the Czarina Catherine, bound for Varna and the Danube, and the group plans a land journey to intercept it. Mina has bound Jonathan to secrecy and insisted on joining the group, as the Count can compel her; the group is now preparing to depart.

Mina wakes and asks Jonathan to promise, on his honour, not to tell her any of the group's plans against the Count, and he agrees. Later she asks to be brought Van Helsing and insists on accompanying them, explaining that the Count can compel her to act and that she may be a help to them. Van Helsing agrees she shall come, and the men gather to plan the Varna journey. Van Helsing lays out the plan: board the ship, find the box, place wild rose on it, and open it when none are watching. Morris vows to destroy the box at once. Van Helsing urges everyone to put their affairs in order, as no one knows how the end will come. Jonathan writes his will, making Mina his sole heir, and watches for Mina's uneasiness at sunset.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XXIV DR. SEWARD’S PHONOGRAPH DIARY, SPOKEN BY VAN HELSING

recaps.text: Before sunset, Mrs. Harker asks her husband and the men to promise they will kill her if she becomes too changed, and each swears. She asks that her husband read the Burial Service over her, and he reads it through tears. Van Helsing hypnotises Mina at dawn and dusk, and she reports only waves, wind and the ship's motion, suggesting it is still at sea. The men plan to board the ship between sunrise and sunset, when the Count cannot act, and open his box.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XXV DR. SEWARD’S DIARY

recaps.text: Count Dracula fled London by sea on the Czarina Catherine, and the group, led by Van Helsing, has been waiting for the ship's arrival at Varna. The ship's delayed journey and Mina's trance reports of waves and motion have kept them uneasy. Now the Czarina Catherine is reported at Galatz, and the group is preparing to travel overland by train the next morning to intercept it. Mina, who is changing and is kept from their plans, seems freer and more hopeful, while Van Helsing privately believes her trance may have given them an advantage over the Count, and keeps the trance from her.

The group receives news that the Czarina Catherine has reached Galatz, which they had half expected as the delay at Varna suggested a change. Mina reveals she knows the train times and that the next train to Galatz leaves at 6:30 the next morning. Van Helsing divides the tasks: Godalming gets tickets, Harker gets letters for the ship's agent, Morris speaks to the Vice-Consul, and Seward stays to consult.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XXV DR. SEWARD’S DIARY

recaps.text: Van Helsing reads typed pages and praises a half-formed thought about the Count's criminal nature, then asks Mina to speak freely. Mina argues the Count is a selfish criminal of limited mind who flees when cornered, as he did from Turkey Land and now from London. She says his hold over her weakened after the blood exchange, though she fears he may have used her knowledge in trance.

Jonathan and Lord Godalming steam up the river in the launch through the night, searching the river for the boat carrying the Count's box. On 31 October and 1 November they inspect boats, taking on a Roumanian flag to smooth their passage, and find nothing matching the box. Dr. Seward and Mr. Morris ride along the right bank, while on the road they learn that the launch was delayed by an accident at rapids.

recaps.text: Mina and Van Helsing wait in a rock shelter as the pursuers converge on the gypsy cart in the snow. Jonathan, Lord Godalming, Dr. Seward and Mr. Morris halt the gypsies with rifles. The Count crumbles into dust, and his face holds an unexpected look of peace. The gypsies flee, and the wolves follow them away, leaving the group alone beneath the castle.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XXVII MINA HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Mr. Morris, bleeding badly from a wound to his side, is helped by Dr. Seward and the others as Jonathan supports him. Morris, holding Mina's hand, cries out that the sacrifice was worth it and points to her forehead, which the sunset lights rosily. The men kneel and give a fervent Amen, and Morris declares that the curse has passed away. Morris smiles and dies quietly, and the group mourns him as a gallant gentleman.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XXVII MINA HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Count Dracula fled London by sea, and the group split to pursue him by river and land. Mina and Van Helsing destroyed the Un-Dead women and banished the Count from his tomb, while Morris died after his wound. This passage jumps seven years ahead: the survivors are settled and happy, and have revisited Transylvania. Their record of events is unverified, and they choose to accept that proof is not needed.
